newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Manufacturers hard hit by NZ dollar - NZIER survey.
newsitem.headline: Manufacturers hard hit by NZ dollar - NZIER survey.

text.p: A cautious sense of business optimism returned in the December quarter, but manufacturers continued to be hard hit by the strong New Zealand dollar, the NZ Institute of Economic Research said in its Quarterly Survey of Business Opinion released on Friday.
The decline in selling prices of manufacturing and building firms that are exporting was the biggest since the series began in 1980, NZIER said on Friday.
Manufacturers reported a prolonged slowdown, but that output had yet to fall as much as in other manufacturing downturns, NZIER said.
Confidence had lifted slightly, consolidating on the gain made in the previous survey.
Firms expecting an improvement in the general business situation during the next six months now outweighed those expecting a deterioration.
"While confidence has improved, the survey provides mixed signals about the state of the economy," NZIER said.
Services' sales began to improve in the quarter, but manufactured exports continued to decline.
Persistent increases in costs matched by falling prices further decreased profitability.
All sectors except builders reported a fall in employment and economy-wide employment was expected to fall further in the next quarter.
While investment in plant and machinery was expected to remain constant over the next year, firms expected investment in buildings to decline.

"The continued high level of the exchange rate must pose a threat to any immediate growth prospects in the manufacturing sector," NZIER said. "Indeed, manufacturing continues to be the weakest sector, with output falling for the third quarter in a row, driven by falling domestic and overseas sales."
While the drop in manufacturers' output was not yet as severe as in previous downturns, the slowdown period had been more prolonged, partly reflecting the Reserve Bank's tight monetary policy.

"In spite of the downturn, manufacturers are optimistic about future output growth. Yet the continued reduction in new orders, when coupled with an overvalued exchange rate, does not bode well for a quick recovery in this sector."

NZIER said the survey indicated the tentative beginnings of an economic upturn, it may be that some quarters yet before the economy shows any signs of renewed growth. NZIER estimated that over three quarters of returns to the survey were completed before the coalition government was formed.
